messages:
jin: FYI: I ran the tiny-stream microbench and saw intermittent p99 spikes (~30-40ms) only when prefetch is enabled. pattern looks like a "double decision" problem between the broker and the coalescer.

rachel: double decision = both sides making idempotent-sounding choices that race? can you sketch sequence?

jin: simplified: Producer enqueues -> Broker prefetch issues a fast lease (side-effect) -> Coalescer starts slack_ms window (e.g. 5ms) to wait for more arrivals -> A second tiny request races in and wins batch ownership -> original fast-lease ends up unused or causes an extra scheduling hop when reassigned. net: extra hop + context switch.

omar: sounds familiar. our current API `acquire_lease()` is mutating and leaks internal scheduling state. that makes composition with a separate batching timer fragile.

kevin: proposal: move to a declarative two-phase handshake: Offer (read-only visibility) + Commit (allocate credits). Offer returns a compact token with TTL and metadata; Commit converts token -> real lease. Offers expire cheaply.

jin: benefits: single source-of-truth for "visibility" of pending work, allows coalescer to observe outstanding offers and make deterministic decisions, prevents accidental double-alloc.

rachel: how to avoid extra RTT on happy path? we can't add an RPC hop for single-request latency.

kevin: Enqueue can return an Offer inline. If coalescer decides to flush immediately, Commit is performed inline (no extra network hop). only workflows that defer require a separate Commit. so common-case stays same.

omar: controls needed: per-tenant max_offers (bounded queue) to avoid memory churn, offer_priority so acceptance favors small/urgent requests, and offer_deadline_ms with bypass policy to prevent tail amplification.

jin: add `slack_ms` as a coordination knob: coalescer waits up to slack_ms but uses randomized jitter to avoid synchronized spikes. offers include a size_hint so coalescer can prefer forming larger batches when helpful.

rachel: failure modes? what if producers spam offers then disappear?

kevin: server-side ringbuffer + expiry sweep solves GC. also return `offer_rejected` when tenant queue full. clients can backoff. surface `broker.offer_queue_depth{tenant}` metric.

omar: fallback path: if Commit latency crosses `offer_deadline_ms`, admission should be allowed to allocate a cold lease directly (bypass) to keep p99 bounded. default bypass=true.

jin: short-term mitigation if we can't ship full Offer/Commit: make `acquire_lease()` return a `churn_score` hint while coalesce window active; callers with high churn_score avoid aggressive prefetch. hacky but quick.

kevin: testing plan: unit tests for offer expiry/claim semantics; microbench harness replaying 1-4 token streams; canary with slack_ms tuned (3-8ms) and compare p50/p95/p99.

rachel: I'll draft a short RFC with proto examples and sequence diagram today. Omar/Keven, can you prototype server-side ringbuffer + compact Offer token?

omar: yep, I'll take ringbuffer + metrics.

kevin: I'll prototype Offer/Commit proto + client piggyback on enqueue.
